description:
Milkweed (Asclepias spp.) is a highly toxic plant for cats. All parts of the plant, including dried leaves and stems, contain powerful toxins called cardiac glycosides. The highest concentration is found in the plant's milky sap.

These toxins directly attack the heart by disrupting the normal electrical signals that control heartbeats. This forces the heart muscle to beat harder but at an abnormal rhythm, which can be very dangerous. The sap can also irritate the digestive system.

If a cat eats milkweed or licks the sap, they may vomit, have diarrhea, or act weak and uncoordinated. More severe signs include difficulty breathing, muscle tremors, and irregular heartbeats. Because heart-related poisoning can worsen very quickly, contact a veterinarian immediately if you suspect your cat has been exposed.
name: Milkweed
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: cardenolide cardiac glycosides in latex sap, leaves, and stems
Mechanism: cardenolides inhibit the Na+/K+-ATPase pump in cardiac muscle cells, causing arrhythmias
Symptoms: drooling, vomiting, weakness, abnormal heart rate, muscle tremors; severe cases may cause seizures and cardiac failure
The milky latex sap is the most concentrated source — avoid contact with broken stems
Seek veterinary care promptly; cardiac glycoside toxicity can escalate rapidly

symptoms.name: Abnormal heart rates and rhythms (including bradycardia, tachycardia, and severe arrhythmias)
Breathing difficulties (dyspnea)
symptoms.onset: Within 2 hours (or developing as the condition worsens).

symptoms.name: Organ damage
symptoms.onset: Delayed (typically develops as symptoms persist over 4–5 days).
